name: Mercat de Forada
desc: The island's most local market, in the field by Can Tixedó Art Café: farm fruit and veg, homemade food, crafts, a book swap, kids' zone, vegan paella at 13:00 and the odd live set. Coffee at Tixedó after.

name: Sant Joan Sunday market
desc: The north's Sunday ritual: the village street filled with island produce, bread, cheese, crafts and clothes, live music on the square and lunch at one of the bars. Runs through the winter — the island's best Sunday out.

name: Las Dalias
desc: The original hippy market, since 1985. In winter it shrinks to Saturdays only and goes back to being what it was: stalls under the trees, a bar, music, no coach parties. Shut for the whole of January; back the first Saturday of February.

name: Rastro de Sant Jordi
desc: The island's flea market around the old racetrack: second-hand everything, vinyl, furniture, bikes, and the best people-watching on Ibiza. Go early.

name: Mercat de sa Cooperativa
village: Sant Antoni, at the Cooperativa (by the Lidl)
desc: The farmers of Sant Antoni selling what they picked that morning: vegetables, fruit, eggs, bread still warm, honey, the island's certified organic growers. The one market where you shop like you live here — go before 11 and bring a bag.

name: Saturdays at Juntos Farm
village: Santa Gertrudis, on the road to Sant Llorenç
desc: A working organic farm with a shop and a tasting room: their own vegetables, goat cheese, honey, soups, preserves, and a buffet breakfast and lunch in winter. Saturdays turn into a small gathering — workshops, talks, farm tours, traditional games and a kids' craft corner. Not a market so much as a place to spend the morning.
